blockers.title: authenticatedKernelMember lost its authenticated-manifest and same-byte joins
evidence: v34 required authenticatedKernelMember.relativePath to select the unique regular-file authenticatedManifest member, required authenticatedKernelMember.sha256 to equal that member's sha256, and required peCoffImageDigest to be computed from those same exact member bytes.

v35 replaces that clause to add kexecCapability but drops all three normative joins. The live authenticatedManifest remains a closed list of only {relativePath, sha256}; no live rule now says authenticatedKernelMember.sha256 MUST equal the selected manifest member's sha256. A search of the live contract finds no authenticatedKernelMember.sha256 equality at all.

peCoffImageDigestAlgorithm names 'exact file bytes of authenticatedKernelMember' as input, but v35 no longer establishes which authenticated-manifest bytes that phrase denotes and never states that the algorithm's output MUST equal authenticatedKernelMember.peCoffImageDigest. The remaining explicit equality is only kernelEvent.digestSha256 == authenticatedKernelMember.peCoffImageDigest.

The imageSignature rule verifies that the record's PE image is accepted by measured db. Secure-Boot signature acceptance is not equality to the exact OS-ABI package member in the signed inventory. packagePayloadDigest can authenticate package A while the boot event and PE signature describe a different db-authorized image M.

Concrete counterexample: the signed entry and authenticatedManifest describe archive A with allowlisted kernel K at a real relativePath; firmware launches different db-authorized M; the observed record uses K's path so one path exists but supplies M's peCoffImageDigest. kernelEvent and imageSignature pass for M, while the package subject and packagePayloadDigest pass for A. The deleted path+hash and same-byte MUSTs provide no refusal, so undeclared M is accepted as the OS ABI.
This is a regression inside the declared v35 roster, not a predecessor-custody issue. The source requirement is exact allowlist identity, not any image accepted by a platform signature key.
blockers.impact: The Linux pathless ceremony can authenticate one package while accepting a different db-signed firmware-launched kernel. The core OS-ABI object authenticity bind is open before any post-boot replacement question is considered, violating NT-TCB-1/3 and the closed host-ABI TCB requirement.
blockers.requiredRepair: Restore explicit MUSTs that relativePath selects exactly one regular-file authenticatedManifest member, sha256 equals that same member's sha256, peCoffImageDigest is recomputed from those same exact member bytes, and the recomputed output equals both authenticatedKernelMember.peCoffImageDigest and kernelEvent.digestSha256. Keep kexec capability evidence separate from, and additionally bound to, that exact member.

blockers.title: A missing kexec_load_disabled sysctl does not prove that kexec is structurally absent
evidence: v35 adds the literal token kexec-absent to authenticatedKernelMember, but authenticatedManifest signs/derives only {relativePath, sha256}. No signed build manifest, kernel configuration, feature measurement, or deterministic inspection procedure derives kexecCapability from the exact authenticated kernel bytes.

The sole operational corroboration is absence of /proc/sys/kernel/kexec_load_disabled in the executing kernel. That filesystem node is an interface exported by a particular kexec/sysctl implementation; absence is not the inverse proof that every legacy kexec_load, kexec_file_load, architecture-specific, or other kernel-replacement path is absent.

A kexec-capable kernel can lack that node because the sysctl is not registered or exposed, the proc/sys view is unavailable or hidden, or the kernel predates the interface. kexec_loaded absent or equal to zero proves at most that the current view does not report a staged image; it does not prove that no image can be loaded after qualification.

The checked path is also a current-kernel, current-namespace self-report. The subject continues to state that its boot evidence does not authenticate the executing image after replacement. A current M with the node absent cannot prove that firmware-launched K lacked kexec, and an observer in a masked procfs view can produce the same absence.

Concrete counterexample independent of B1: restore the exact K-to-manifest join, then use an allowlisted K that has functional kexec but no exposed kexec_load_disabled node. The unsupported observed token says kexec-absent, the required path is absent, and kexec_loaded is absent or zero, so every v35 pass condition holds. K can nevertheless load and enter undeclared M after qualification.

G22 remains NAMED-NOT-QUALIFIED and its kexec-unavailable lab precondition explicitly is not cryptographic proof. There is therefore no qualified harness evidence that can convert the negative pathname observation into the claimed structural capability.
blockers.impact: A replacement-capable Linux kernel can qualify as kexec-absent and later enter an undeclared kernel. The claimed no-replacement policy admits false assurance and does not close PTCB-V34-B2 or the current OS-ABI TCB.
blockers.requiredRepair: Define a closed kexec-capability evidence object cryptographically bound to the same exact authenticated kernel member. It must enumerate and prove absence of every supported replacement entry point using signed build configuration/provenance or another independently verifiable procedure, with observer namespace and failure semantics fixed. Treat procfs presence/absence only as corroboration, never as the structural proof. Alternatively authenticate the current kernel independently and compare its exact identity to the signed inventory.

shouldFix.title: Removing OptionalData security also removed the only EFI_LOAD_OPTION parser needed for FilePathList
evidence: v35 correctly withdraws OptionalData tokens as security facts, eliminating the v34 UTF-8 command-line defect. It also deletes fromBootLockdown.loadOptionParse, and no other live EFI_LOAD_OPTION structural parser remains.

FilePathList is still expressly retained as the authenticated configured boot target from raw Boot#### VariableData and remains load-bearing in inScopeBootConfigs. Extracting it requires parsing EFI_LOAD_OPTION attributes, FilePathListLength, the terminated CHAR16 Description, and the bounded device-path byte region.

Without the deleted bounds and truncation rules, validators can disagree on malformed Description or FilePathListLength inputs even though the measured bytes are identical. The v35 refusal summaries also remove malformed EFI_LOAD_OPTION from the fail-closed list.

OptionalData encoding need not be specified when its contents are non-security metadata, but that does not remove the need to locate and validate the preceding FilePathList security field deterministically.
shouldFix.impact: Independent implementations can derive different authenticated boot targets from the same measured Boot#### bytes or fail to reject malformed load options, weakening deterministic handoff review even after the kernel byte join is restored.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Restore the v34 structural EFI_LOAD_OPTION parser and malformed-input refusal solely for extracting FilePathList. Keep OptionalData opaque and non-security-bearing; do not restore the UTF-8 token policy.

verdictBasis: REJECT because ACCEPT requires 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX; this review finds 2 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX finding.
conclusion: REJECT. v35 reproduces its custody pins, fixes the v34 roster and pre-kernel class-map defects, and withdraws OptionalData tokens as a security mechanism. It regresses the core pathless kernel bind by deleting the explicit authenticated-manifest path+hash and same-byte PE digest equalities. Its replacement policy is also an unsupported kexec-absent token corroborated only by absence of a current procfs node, which does not prove structural absence of every kexec path. Finally, FilePathList remains security-bearing after the only EFI_LOAD_OPTION parser was removed. DR-126 remains OPEN; Linux remains in D-002 slice 1; no DR is marked SATISFIED, and no D-096 (A) grant, application, sealing, or implementation authority is created.
